termsPageDescription: Where the data comes from, its licence and its limits, and how to have it corrected or a file taken down.
termsSources: The catalog is compiled from public sources: vendor websites, press releases, product catalogs and datasheets. Every value cites its source. Values are given as published, with no warranty that they are accurate, complete or fit for a purpose: verify a value with its vendor before you rely on it.
termsLicence: The catalog's data is licensed under {licence}. You may share and adapt it for non-commercial use if you credit {brand}, link to the product's page and keep the link to each vendor source. Commercial use needs a licence from {brand}. The site's code is not licensed.
termsMedia: Datasheets, manuals, images, videos, product names and trademarks belong to their owners; the data licence does not cover them. A file under a vendor's copyright is stored privately and never served by the site: its page links to the vendor's own copy. Only files that are the site's own or openly licensed are served from the site. Summaries are written in the site's own words.
termsCorrections: Corrections, takedown notices and commercial licence requests go through “{report}” on a product's page. Say what is wrong, or which file or value a takedown concerns and the right you hold, and how to reach you. Every report goes to the review queue; nothing changes until an editor approves it. A file taken down is deleted from storage; the product's record stays.
privacyPageDescription: What the site sends, what it keeps, where, and for how long.
privacyBrowser: The site sets no cookies and runs no analytics or advertising trackers. Your browser keeps your language, theme and compare list in its own storage. The words you search go to the site's server, which ranks the products and keeps nothing of the words.
privacyCounts: The site counts searches, searches with no result, clicks on a result, questions answered and refused, and visits from AI assistants, as totals per day, with no search words, IP address or identifier. The first count of a visit carries the address of the page you came from; only an AI assistant's name is kept from it.
privacyAsk: A question asked on Ask is sent, with its language, to the site's server. Unless the same question was answered before, the server sends it, with the catalog records it matches, to Muse Spark, Meta's model, through the Meta Model API in its Standard mode, in which Meta does not use what it is sent to train its models. The server keeps the answer, under a digest of the question's words, to give it again; each visitor's count of questions for the day, under a digest of the IP address and the day, which changes every day, to apply the daily limit; and for each model call its model, tokens, cost, duration and outcome, with no question, answer or address. These records have no set deletion date.
privacyReport: “{report}” on a product page sends the product, your message and the source link if you give one to the site's server, which files them with the time in the review queue, in Firestore. Opening the form loads Google reCAPTCHA through Firebase App Check, and sending the report runs it: it reads signals from your browser and device, may keep some in your browser's storage, and Google processes them under its own privacy policy (policies.google.com/privacy). The report asks for no name or email address and stores no IP address. Only the site's editor reads the queue. Reports, with whatever their message holds, are kept with the queue's history, with no set deletion date.
privacyAdmin: Only the site's editor works at /admin. Signing in there goes through Firebase Authentication with a Google account: Firebase keeps the email address, name and sign-in dates of each account that signs in, and the session in that browser. The public pages have no accounts and no sign-in.
privacyProviders: The site runs on Google's Firebase and Google Cloud, and Google processes these requests for it: Hosting serves the pages; Firestore holds the catalog, the review queue and the records above; Cloud Storage holds the search index and files; Cloud Functions runs the server; App Check checks that a report comes from the site's form; Authentication signs the editor in. Firestore, Cloud Storage and the server are in Google Cloud's us-central1 region (United States). Meta runs the Ask model, through the Meta Model API. Google Cloud's request logs for the server record each request's IP address, kept for the retention period set in Google Cloud.
privacyRequests: For a question about this data, or to have it removed, use “{report}” on any product page.
